note: Search by meaning is one setting on the same memory search that the per-person memory card switches on (the provider key moves from keyword-only to an embedding model on the Mac mini); its 'later' wave rested on priority and not on a dependency or a new kind of risk, and no earlier merge pass ruled on the pair, so it becomes a named later, optional step on the wave A memory card, which ships on keyword search and keeps the medium risk.

record.name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' is saved to that parent's own notes and found again, by keyword first and by meaning as a later step
record.description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent writes the fact to its notes and finds it again in later chats; where those notes live is an open decision that settles whether a saved note survives the next deploy and whether it is in view at the start of a chat or found only when Happy searches. Notes are found by their words at first; a later, optional step adds search by meaning for text notes, with the indexing done on the Mac mini.
record.example: Jordan texts: 'Remember that piano moved to Thursdays at 4.' A week later she asks 'which day is piano?' and gets Thursday at 4. After the later step, 'what was the kid's nut thing again?' finds the note that says 'tree-nut allergy', although none of the words match.
record.how: Notes (F041): allow write and edit on each parent's agent, with a read-write workspace and apply_patch denied by name; an in-house before_tool_call hook limits write paths, by default to memory/*.md (MEMORY.md and USER.md stay with the F042 generator unless a live test shows a chat write does not stop them loading); memory_search and memory_get with keyword-only search set explicitly (`memory.search.provider: "none"`; unset, the documented default is OpenAI embeddings); the bundled session-memory hook. Later step (F046): install the official llama.cpp provider plugin, run its embedding-only setup, set the provider to `local` with `fallback: "none"` and re-index; the same search also covers the family handbook (F043). Further option: Active Memory, which adds a blocking model call to each reply it runs on.
depends_on: Decision: where chat-saved notes live. Working default: memory/*.md only, because a chat write to MEMORY.md or USER.md can stop that file, and the family facts F042 renders into it, from loading at the start of a chat (see caveats)
An in-house before_tool_call hook that limits write and edit to the chosen memory files, proven with a test write outside them; apply_patch denied by name
memory_search and memory_get allowed on each parent's agent, with keyword-only search

A live test for each parent before go-live: save a note, start a new chat, and check that the note is found and that the family facts still load; include one note saved in Chinese. For Jordan the result may turn on whether she is made a command owner, the decision listed under timed reminders (F007)
Later step only: the official llama.cpp provider plugin and a small embedding model downloaded to the Mac mini; whether and when to install them is Tony's call
Later step only, optional: F043 family handbook, if its pages are to be searched by meaning too (saving and finding per-person notes does not need it)
caveats: Where chat-saved notes live is undecided: as read in the installed docs and code and not tried on a live turn, a chat write to MEMORY.md or USER.md from a sender who is not the command owner (today every turn of Jordan's), after web content in the same turn, or after the family-facts generator (F042) has re-rendered the file marks the whole file untrusted, and an untrusted file no longer loads at the start of a chat, the generated family facts in it included.

Keeping saved notes in memory/*.md avoids that at a cost: only today's and yesterday's dated notes load at a fresh start and older ones are found only when the agent searches, so until the choice is made and tested for both parents a saved note is not guaranteed to come back.

MEMORY.md is loaded at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat but not in scheduled jobs, group chats or hand-offs to a helper, so a brief or a reminder does not know a saved note unless its job is given memory search.

Refusing a memory write in a turn that carried web or research results is not something the platform does for a file write: no taint flag that a hook can read was found, so the in-house hook has to track web tool calls itself, and this is untested.
Notes belong to one parent; something both parents should get the same answer to belongs in the household store (F031) or the family handbook (F043).
Until the later step is done a saved note is found by its words and not by its meaning, and whether keyword search finds a note saved in Chinese on the default index setting has not been tested.

Search by meaning covers text only, because on this version photo and audio indexing works only with Google's cloud embedding model, and how much it would improve on keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a measured figure.
If the embedding server on the Mac mini fails, search drops back to keyword matching without telling the parent; the reason shows only in a debug field.
record.safety: Notes stay in each parent's own agent; shared agents such as research hold none. A fail-closed before_tool_call hook limits writes to the memory files, and apply_patch is denied by name. A saved note is where an injected instruction could persist; the weekly review (G006) shows what was saved. The later step embeds on the Mac mini with no cloud fallback and adds no tool or send path.

note: The emergency plan, the sitter sheet and the school, camp and health-form kit all draw on the same children's facts (contacts, allergies, medicines) kept in the shared family folder and are prompt rules on the parent's own agent with nothing sent by Happy, so they become one wave B card on which those facts are entered once (the kit's wave C had no later dependency behind it and no earlier merge pass ruled on the pair); the fixed emergency reply and the form kit are stated as separate parts, and effort rises to M for two small halves.

record.name: Emergency card, sitter sheet and school and camp form kit from one set of family facts, plus a fixed reply to emergency texts
record.description: From one set of family facts in the shared family folder, Happy helps a parent produce the pages other people ask for: a one-page emergency plan to print, a sitter or grandparent sheet to forward, and, for school, camp and sports forms, an index of where each document is and when it stops being accepted, a warning before a form is due and the answers as one copy-paste block; the parent prints, forwards, signs and submits. Happy is never the emergency channel: a text that contains one of a short list of emergency phrases gets one fixed call-emergency-services line at once, without a model, as a backstop and not a detector.
record.example: A parent texts 'make the sitter sheet for Friday' and gets one message to forward or print. Jordan texts: 'Camp forms for both kids are due May 1. What do I still need?' A parent who texts 'He swallowed something, what do I do?' gets the fixed call-emergency-services line immediately.
record.how: Facts: a plan page and a page per child in the shared family folder (F043), entered once. Emergency plan (CRT-13): an interview on the parent's agent following Ready.gov's four steps, with a yearly reminder to re-check contacts. Sitter sheet (F036): a prompt template in AGENTS.md over the same facts. Form kit (CRT-12): the child's page also records where each official document lives and when it stops being accepted; a household-store row per form (F031) is the checklist, the due-date warning is a timed reminder (F007) offered through the dates-after-a-yes flow (F010), and a form sent as a photo or PDF (F002) gets its answers drafted as one block under a drafts-only rule. Fixed reply: the stop plugin's (G005) `before_dispatch` hook matches a short phrase list and returns a canned line before any model call.
depends_on: F043 family folder (the plan page and the per-child pages)
G005 stop-by-text plugin (the fixed reply shares its hook)
F007 reminders (the yearly contact re-check and the form due dates)
F031 household store (one dated row per form)
F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments on, for a form sent as a photo or PDF
F010 dates-after-a-yes flow (offers the reminder for a form's due date; until it exists a parent asks for a timed reminder directly)
F009 calendar read (only for 'tonight's plan' on the sitter sheet)
F080 print, optional: until it exists a parent prints the page from a phone
caveats: Happy can be down in exactly the events that matter, since a power cut stops the Mac and a network outage stops iMessage, so the printed sheet is the part that survives, and the phone's own emergency call and medical ID features remain the right tools.
Phrase matching will fire on jokes and miss paraphrases, and the hook that does it lets the text through to the model if it fails, so the fixed reply is a backstop and must be harmless when wrong.
The poison-help number in the fixed reply comes from the poison centre's own page listed in the sources, and a parent checks it before the reply goes live.

A stop by text or a lock-out (G005) and the quiet hours and daily caps (G001) must never hold the fixed reply back: the emergency phrases are checked before the stop file, whether a locked-out handle still gets the line is a choice to write down, and all of it is tested with a stop in force.
The children's health facts (allergies, medicines, conditions) reach the cloud model whenever a sheet or an answer block is drafted, and they stay out of hand-offs to the research agent.
Happy never signs, fills in or submits a form; the drafts-only rule is a prompt instruction that holds only because the agent has no tool that could fill in or send one.

Requirements differ by state, district and camp: Happy tracks what each form asked for last time and does not know the rules, and the official immunization record has to come from the doctor, the state registry or the school, since portal logins are out of scope.

Keep ID, policy and certificate numbers and the Wi-Fi password off these pages, and keep expiry dates in the renewals look-ahead (F063) and form due dates in timed reminders (F007, F010), so nothing is tracked twice.
record.safety: The fixed reply is a string the parents wrote, sent only to the sender: no tool, no data, no model. The pages hold contacts and the children's health facts; they stay in the private family folder and on paper, and drafting from them sends those facts to the cloud model. Happy messages nobody outside the family: a parent forwards the sheet and submits every form.
